- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add slight upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out abrupt changes in forecast slope.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (0.00) followed by a spike, model often misses the rebound; anticipate 1–2 days of upward correction.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 18-day average unless sentiment strongly supports it; use sentiment as a floor/ceiling trigger.
